notes: Prompts are paraphrased from real sessions (6-10 Nov 2026, Newcastle career, in-game date about 11 Nov 2030). None needs a match in progress. 'required' lists the human-readable content a good answer must have; 'checks' are the deterministic subset used by score.mjs (types: regex, notRegex, names, rows, firstChars, date, minChars; add soft:true to report without failing). Specific player names are taken from the real save and may need updating if the career moves on. Version 2 (11 Nov 2026, game date 10 Dec 2030): board confidence, inbox, calendar, player status and club vision became readable through runtime tools, so board-inbox now expects real values; five questions added for those tools, manager-view stars and fm_report. Ground truth on 10 Dec 2030: board overall B ('very pleased'), areas Club Vision C+, Match C, Recruitment B, Tactics C+, Squad B+; next fixtures Villarreal (UCL, away, 10 Dec), West Ham (PL, away, 13 Dec), Bournemouth (Carabao Cup, away, 18 Dec), Crystal Palace (PL, home, 21 Dec), Brighton (PL, away, 26 Dec); inbox includes 'FA Cup draws Newcastle against Wolves'; 3 unhappy players at the club, none in the first team; earliest squad contract expiry 30 June 2032. Version 3 (12 Nov 2026, game date 13 Dec 2030): ground truth that moves with the game is read at run time by evals/facts.mjs into the run's facts.json; a check pattern names a fact as {{key}} and score.mjs substitutes it (a missing fact makes that check soft). Six questions added: three management decisions that test the answer contract (decision first, compact evidence with benchmarks, what would change it) and three that catch a silent full-view answer about another club's hidden data (balance, wages); check type 'transcript' inspects the SQL the run sent. 12 Nov 2026: decision-first cues accept "prioritise"; the match-day XI counts squad surnames from facts; benchmark cues accept a named peer ("versus X") and per-game rates; what-changes cues accept unverified/unchecked and conditional triggers. Version 4 (12 Nov 2026, adviser 1.4.0, reader round 2, game date 13 Dec 2030): eleven questions on the new surface (rating components, promises, hierarchy and social groups, career histories, agent demands, finance breakdown, registration, attribute history, competition history, and two manager-view questions whose answers are now public: another club's wages and a rival player's contract expiry). Other clubs' players' wages and contract expiry became public in the manager view, so leak-cb-wage-search no longer expects 'wages are hidden' and leak-rival-player-wage now expects the actual wage and expiry from the manager view; a release clause, a rival's balance or an exact hidden attribute is still a leak (score.mjs HIDDEN_COLS).

questions.prompt: Assuming I play a 4-2-3-1, which positions should I pursue depth at? Rank your top three and say why, using my current squad.
required: Opens with a ranked recommendation, not a preamble
Names exactly the three highest-priority positions or slots in 4-2-3-1 terms
Cites named current players (with age or contract) as evidence for each gap
States the game date the data was read at

checks.desc: cites at least 4 named players (name heuristic: misses surnames)
cites at least 4 current squad players by name

questions.prompt: Find me a goalkeeper to eventually succeed Kobel, even if it's not this year. Give me a shortlist with age, club, contract situation and why each one fits.
required: Mentions Kobel's age/contract to frame the succession window
Shortlist of at least 3 named goalkeepers, each with club and age
Contract situation or cost indication per candidate
Says which one to prioritise
Separates facts read from the save from judgement

checks.desc: at least 3 candidates plus Kobel named

questions.prompt: Search the whole save for left-backs aged 21 or younger who could realistically develop into my starter, earning under 60,000 a week. Give me the best five with club, age, wage and the attributes that make them interesting.
required: Searches beyond Newcastle (save-wide), not just the club's own squad
At least 3 named players with club and age, all aged 21 or younger
States wage for each and whether it is under the cap, or says wage is unavailable
States how the search was scoped and whether the result is complete or a sample
Does not present estimated or hidden attributes as certain

questions.prompt: Write profiles of my two right-backs and explain how they differ and when I should pick each one.
required: Identifies exactly the club's two right-backs by name
Describes each as a footballer in plain language, not a dump of attribute numbers
Explains the difference and gives usage guidance per match situation or opponent type
Mentions age, contract or fitness where relevant

questions.prompt: Give me a tier list of the players in my first-team squad: who is elite, good, solid, and who is a weak link. Base it on this season's performances and ability, and say which ratings are your judgement.
required: Covers the whole first-team squad, not a handful of players
Clear tiers with players assigned to each
Uses evidence (ratings, minutes, ability) rather than only reputation
Flags the weak links and what to do about them
Distinguishes measured data from judgement

questions.prompt: Which players in my squad have contracts expiring within the next 12 months, what do they earn, and who should I renew first? Include their agreed playing time status if you can see it.
required: States the game date used for 'next 12 months'
Lists each expiring player with expiry date and wage, or says plainly that none expire in the window (on 10 Dec 2030 the earliest squad expiry is 30 June 2032)
Gives a renewal priority order with reasoning (for the earliest expiries when none fall in the window)
Does not invent playing-time promises when the field is unavailable

checks.desc: names the players whose contracts expire within 12 months, or says none

questions.prompt: Where do we stand on FFP and wage budget right now, and if we need to clear room, how would you do it?
required: States current finance position with figures and where they were read from
Says plainly which figures are unavailable or unsupported rather than guessing
Offers concrete, named actions to create room (sales, loans, contract changes) with approximate effect
Leads with the conclusion

questions.prompt: Can you see Manchester United's FFP situation, and how does it compare to ours?
required: Either gives sourced comparative figures for both clubs or clearly says what cannot be read for the rival
Does not fabricate rival financial figures
Says which fields it could compare and which it could not

checks.desc: does not quote United figures hidden from the manager

questions.prompt: What does my club actually know about Morten Hjulmand right now? Are his attributes fully scouted or estimated, how reliable is that, and what would you do to firm it up?
required: Distinguishes true attributes from what my scouts and staff can see (knowledge level, estimated ranges, hidden or unscouted fields)
Says how reliable the information is and why
Concrete next step to improve knowledge (scout assignment, watch live, shortlist)
Does not present estimated values as exact

questions.prompt: Who are the top five scorers in the Premier League this season, with their clubs and goals?
required: Exactly five (or clearly labelled top-N) players with club and goal count
States the date or number of matches the table reflects
Says if the list is complete or limited by data coverage
Answers in a compact table or list near the top

checks.desc: names the actual top scorers read at run time

questions.prompt: What are the toughest parts of my fixture list over the next two months, and where should I plan rotation?
required: Dated fixture window with opponents and competitions
Identifies the hardest run and says why (opposition strength, congestion, travel)
Suggests specific rotation points or player management
States the game date the window starts from

questions.prompt: Who in my Newcastle squad is agreed Regular Starter or above, and which of them actually started the fewest of my last five completed Premier League matches?
required: Lists players whose agreed playing time is Regular Starter or above
Counts starts over the last five completed Premier League matches, with the fixtures identified
Names the player(s) with fewest starts and the numbers
States data limits (for example unknown promise field or missing lineups)

questions.prompt: Review our most recent completed Premier League match. What decided it, who was best and worst, and what should we change next time?
required: Names the opponent, score and date of the match
Supports claims with match data (shots, xG, possession, ratings, passing) and says which stats were available
Names best and worst performers
Gives at least two concrete changes
Says what the data could not show

checks.desc: reviews the most recent Premier League match

questions.prompt: Scout my next Premier League opponent: how will they likely set up, who are their key players, and what plan would you use against them?
required: Names the next Premier League opponent and fixture date
Describes their likely shape and style from data, not stereotypes
Names key opposition players with reasons
Gives a plan for us including who to pick or role changes
States what is inferred rather than observed

questions.prompt: Pick my XI and bench for my next league match based on the matchup and current fitness. Say who you are resting and why.
required: Names a starting eleven in a stated formation
Names a bench
Uses injury, fitness or suspension data and says what was checked
Says who is rested and why
States the opponent and date

checks.desc: names at least 11 squad players (surnames count)

questions.prompt: What is the board's confidence in me right now, and is there anything in my inbox I should deal with?
required: Reports the board's overall grade (B, 'very pleased') from fm_get_board_confidence, with at least one area grade
Names at least one real inbox subject (for example 'FA Cup draws Newcastle against Wolves') from fm_get_inbox
Says what, if anything, needs action
Does not say board confidence or the inbox cannot be read, and does not ask for screenshots

checks.desc: reports the overall grade read at run time
names a word from a current inbox subject
does not claim the data is unreadable

questions.prompt: Show me the shot map from our most recent completed Premier League match: who shot, from where, and what the xG was.
required: Names the opponent, score and date of the match
Uses the retained shot data (a deferred shot-map tool found with tool_search), not a guess
Lists shots or shooters with location or xG, or states exactly which coverage is unavailable

checks.desc: states the match or game date

questions.prompt: What are my next five fixtures?
required: Lists exactly five first-team fixtures in date order with date, opponent, competition and home/away
Matches the calendar: Villarreal (UCL, away, 10 Dec), West Ham (PL, away, 13 Dec), Bournemouth (Carabao Cup, away, 18 Dec), Crystal Palace (PL, home, 21 Dec), Brighton (PL, away, 26 Dec)
Leaves out U21 and U18 fixtures
States the game date

checks.desc: names the next opponents read at run time

questions.prompt: Who in my squad is unhappy and why?
required: Uses fm_get_player_status (and optionally fm_get_club_vision) rather than morale or guesswork
Names each unhappy player found with the game's own reasons, or says plainly that none in the first team is unhappy (on 10 Dec 2030 three players at the club are unhappy, none in the first team)
Says how many players were checked and whether reserves and youth were included
Does not invent promises or complaints

questions.prompt: What does the board expect from me this season, and what is the club vision?
required: Lists the board's objectives with their importance from fm_get_club_vision (for example 'Work within wage budget', Required)
Summarises the board and supporter culture (attacking, entertaining, high-tempo pressing football; set pieces)
Separates the board's objectives from supporters' expectations
Gives a short judgement of where the user stands, labelled as judgement

questions.prompt: What do my scouts think of Kennet Eichhorn's current and potential ability?
required: Answers from the manager's knowledge (fm_db_query view manager on m_player_view, or the deferred visible-attributes tool) and says so

Gives current and potential ability as stars or star ranges, never as CA/PA numbers (on 10 Dec 2030 the manager view shows current 3.5-4.5 stars, potential 3.5-5 stars, 19 attributes exact and 28 ranges)
States how complete the knowledge is (exact, range and unknown attribute counts or similar)
Suggests how to firm it up if the stars are a range

checks.desc: gives the star ranges read at run time

questions.prompt: Give me a shortlist report of young left-backs my scouts know.
required: Uses the manager's knowledge (scouted players), reporting ranges and stars, and says so
Produces an HTML report with fm_report and gives its absolute file path
Gives the top recommendation in the terminal answer as well
States the game date and coverage

checks.pattern: (?:hidden|not (?:visible|public|shown|known|available)|can(?:no|')t see|cannot see|doesn'?t (?:show|know)|manager'?s knowledge|not something (?:you|the manager)|actual values)
